audit_findings.title: Maintenance capex may be understated within unusually heavy expansion spending
audit_findings.mechanism: Underclassified maintenance capital expenditure directly inflates recurring owner earnings and every scenario derived from the $223.5 million anchor.
audit_findings.evidence: Net cash used in investing activities was $178.8 million for fiscal 2026, which was primarily attributable to capital expenditures related to store construction, improvements to our distribution center facilities, and investments in our new Store Support Center.
audit_findings.explanation: No error is yet demonstrated because the maintenance-capex calculation was not supplied. However, FY2026 property-and-equipment purchases were $178.561 million, about 80% of the anchor, and covered stores, distribution facilities, and the Store Support Center. Even a modest recurring-cost misclassification would propagate through the entire DCF and is reasonably capable of materially changing fair value.
audit_findings.action: Reconstruct FY2026 capex by project and asset class, including the $20.551 million of unpaid property purchases, landlord allowances, remodels, fixtures, software, and distribution assets. Recalculate maintenance capex for the 539-store footprint and rerun all scenarios if it differs from the amount used in the anchor.

audit_findings.title: Signed but uncommenced leases create costs absent from current earnings and recorded lease liabilities
audit_findings.magnitude: $157.7 million minimum commitment at June 27, 2026, up from $152.3 million at March 28, 2026; net value effect unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: Once leases commence, rent, variable occupancy expense, and start-up losses reduce owner earnings, while sales and eventual store profits may increase owner earnings and growth.
audit_findings.evidence: As of March 28, 2026, the Company’s minimum lease commitment for operating leases signed but not yet commenced was $ 152.3 million.
audit_findings.explanation: The commitments are demonstrated, but no current valuation error is demonstrated. The stores had not commenced, and the model applies aggregate growth rates rather than explicitly crediting individual openings. Their net effect is forward-looking and depends on commencement timing and store-level economics, so the commitments should not be deducted mechanically from the equity bridge.
audit_findings.action: Obtain the lease commencement schedule and cohort forecasts for rent, common-area charges, pre-opening costs, sales, and store-level profit. Confirm these net effects are represented in the scenario growth paths and rerun any scenario that credits opening-related growth without the corresponding costs.

audit_findings.title: FY2026 margins may not be a sustainable tariff-cost baseline
audit_findings.mechanism: A delayed increase in landed inventory costs would reduce merchandise margin, net income, and recurring owner earnings below the $223.5 million anchor independently of sales growth.
audit_findings.evidence: Changing tariff rates and shifting trade policies have created, and continue to create, significant uncertainty for suppliers, consumers, and us.
audit_findings.explanation: The filing demonstrates tariff uncertainty but does not establish that FY2026 owner earnings contain a tariff timing error or quantify a normalized margin. The following quarter included a separate $14.7 million cost-of-goods-sold benefit from tariff refunds; excluding that benefit, the quarter's computed gross margin was approximately 37.9% versus 39.1% in the prior-year quarter, but the filing attributes the underlying movements to several factors, including freight, occupancy, and product margin. The record therefore cannot isolate or establish the materiality of a tariff-related reset.
audit_findings.action: Trace inventory vintages, duties paid, refund eligibility, landed costs, pricing actions, and sell-through after March 2026. Build a normalized merchandise-margin case excluding tariff refunds and rerun the valuation if normalized recurring owner earnings differ from the anchor.

audit_findings.title: The bridge assumes all cash is surplus to operations
audit_findings.magnitude: $139.262 million maximum bridge exposure ($4.49 per diluted share)
audit_findings.mechanism: Any cash required for seasonal working capital or committed operating needs should remain with the business rather than be added as non-operating value in the equity bridge.
audit_findings.evidence: Our primary cash needs are for inventories, operating expenses, occupancy expenses, capital expenditures associated with opening new stores and remodeling or refurbishing existing stores, improvements to our distribution facilities, marketing and information technology expenditures, debt service and taxes.
audit_findings.explanation: The filings establish substantial seasonal and operating cash needs but do not demonstrate the minimum required cash balance. Nevertheless, even the conservative extreme of treating none of the $139.262 million as surplus would reduce value by only $4.49 per share: bear, base, and bull values would be approximately $85.70, $101.22, and $119.43, respectively. The $154.29 market price would remain above the bull value, so this issue cannot change the valuation conclusion.
audit_findings.action: Calculate minimum operating cash from seasonal cash lows, inventory peaks, near-term capex, lease payments, and revolver availability. Use only the residual excess cash in the bridge; rerun the bridge for precision, although the current investment conclusion will remain unchanged even at the maximum adjustment.
